title: US Returns Artifacts to India
main_content:
The United States has returned more than 200 artifacts to the government of India.

The artifacts were valued at more than $100 million. They had been stolen from India and taken out of the country.

The artifacts included statues and pieces made of bronze and terracotta. Some pieces were more than 2,000 years old.

They were returned to the Indian government Monday at a ceremony in Washington, D.C.

The meeting was attended by U.S. Attorney General Loretta Lynch and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Among the pieces is a statue of Saint Manikkavacakar. That statue was stolen from the Sivan Temple in Chennai, India. It is valued at $1.5 million. Another is a bronze sculpture of the Hindu god Ganesha.

Prime Minister Modi was thankful to the U.S. for returning the artifacts to India.
